rows.title: Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Data Analyst - Online Luxury Retail Company - Up to £150,000
You stop producing dashboards and start shaping the decisions that drive a $10 billion business into new markets.
This company sells premium goods direct from manufacturers, cutting out the middleman entirely. That model has fuelled 130% year-on-year growth and a huge US success story. Now they are building out across Europe, and your work sits at the heart of that expansion.
You join a cross-functional storefront team working directly alongside product, engineering and merchandising. You are not a reporting function here. You run hands-on analysis, build predictive models, design and interpret A/B tests, and translate what you find into real commercial and product decisions. When a new market launches, you are the person identifying what drives conversion, what shapes customer behaviour, and what the team should prioritise next.
The company is deeply data-led. A significant proportion of their people are analysts, and there is a genuine appetite for AI and predictive modelling at every level. You are not pushing for a seat at the table. You already have one.
You define success metrics, uncover growth opportunities and help determine what gets built and when. The influence is real and the visibility is international.
To do this well, you are strong in SQL and bring senior-level experience in analytical roles, ideally within a fast-moving commercial environment. You have done this kind of work before and you want more scope to do it properly.
The role is office based and comes with a salary of up to £150,000, unlimited holiday, pension, and medical and dental cover.
Ready to move beyond reporting and into something that actually moves the needle?
Get in touch.
No up-to-date CV required.

rows.title: Operational Insight and Assurance Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
LOCATION: Heathrow Airport

SHIFT PATTERN: Monday to Friday

SALARY: Competitive

If you require any additional support or adjustments during the recruitment process, please don't hesitate to contact our Recruitment Department at recruitment@abm.com. We're here to help!

Role Overview And Purpose

The Operational Insight & Assurance Analyst will provide independent assurance across operational performance, data and reporting within Aviation and Transport. Sitting within the Business Intelligence team, the role will act as the bridge between frontline operations, data governance and analytical reporting, ensuring that the information used to manage performance accurately reflects what is happening operationally.

The role will combine operational assurance, data validation, analytics and documentation. It will involve working directly with frontline teams as well as BI Analysts, Data Engineers and operational management to validate the full information chain from operational activity and system capture through data ingestion, transformation and final reporting.

Key Responsibilities

The Analyst will carry out operational assurance activity across Aviation and Transport, observing frontline processes and comparing what happens in practice with the information recorded in operational systems. This will include validating operational timestamps, statuses, outcomes and processes, identifying where system data does not accurately represent operational activity, and documenting any control or process weaknesses.

The role will provide independent validation of data and reporting, including source-to-target reconciliation, record-count validation, identification of missing or duplicate records, testing of business rules and calculations, and manual sample validation. The Analyst will support assurance of Power BI reporting, KPI and SLA calculations and other management information by independently reproducing key results and confirming that agreed definitions and methodologies have been applied correctly.

A key part of the role will be tracing operational events through the complete data lifecycle — from the frontline operation, through source systems, ingestion and transformation, to the final dashboard or reported result. This will allow the business to identify where information may have been lost, changed, incorrectly classified or interpreted.

The Analyst will also use data and analytics to identify trends, anomalies and areas requiring further operational investigation. Assurance activity should increasingly be risk-based and data-led, allowing the team to focus attention on areas where there is the greatest potential operational, contractual or reporting impact.

The role will support the development and maintenance of clear documentation including KPI and SLA definitions, data dictionaries, business rules, calculation methodologies, data lineage, validation procedures, QA evidence and Standard Operating Procedures. Documentation and assurance evidence should allow significant reported results to be independently understood and reproduced.

Where issues are identified, the Analyst will support root-cause analysis and corrective action, distinguishing between operational, system, data, transformation and reporting causes. They will work collaboratively with operational, BI and Data Engineering teams to implement preventative controls and improve the quality of data at source rather than relying solely on downstream correction.

Stakeholder Engagement

The role will work across frontline operations, operational management, Business Intelligence, Data Engineering, Performance, Quality and Compliance teams, as well as supporting customer, audit or regulatory requirements where appropriate. A key capability will be translating between operational and technical teams — explaining why a data issue matters operationally and, equally, why an operational process may be creating a data or reporting issue.

Requirements

The successful candidate will have strong analytical and investigative skills, excellent attention to detail and the confidence to challenge data, processes and reported results constructively. They should be comfortable working both with operational teams on the ground and with technical or analytical teams.

Experience working with operational, performance or quality data is essential, together with strong Excel capability and experience validating datasets or calculations. Experience with Power BI, SQL, Microsoft Fabric, Power Query, DAX, data modelling or data-quality frameworks would be advantageous. Aviation, transport or another regulated operational environment would also be beneficial but is not essential.

Measures of Success

Success in the role will be demonstrated through increased confidence in Business Intelligence outputs, improved reproducibility of key reporting, reduction in recurring data-quality issues, stronger documentation and data lineage, effective closure of assurance findings and the identification of operational or data issues before they materially affect contractual, customer, regulatory or management reporting.

rows.title: Exposure Management Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Job Type

Permanent

Build a brilliant future with Hiscox

About Hiscox

As an international specialist insurer, we are far removed from the world of mass-market insurance products. Instead, we are selective and focus on our key areas of expertise and strength, underpinned by a culture that encourages us to challenge convention and always look for a better way of doing things.

We insure the unique and the interesting. And we search for the same when it comes to talented people. Hiscox is full of smart, reliable human beings that look out for customers and each other. We believe in doing the right thing, making good and rebuilding when things go wrong. Everyone is encouraged to think creatively, challenge the status quo and look for solutions.

Scratch beneath the surface and you will find a business that is solid, but slightly contrary. We like to do things differently and constantly seek to evolve. We might have been around for a long time (our roots go back to 1901), but we are young in many ways, ambitious and going places.

Some people might say insurance is dull, but life at Hiscox is anything but. If that sounds good to you, get in touch.

About The Team/division

The Hiscox London Market Exposure Management Team comprises 8 people based in London. The role of the team is to help Hiscox London Market deliver its underwriting goals by controlling the level of exposures across multiple Lines of Business. The team is highly motivated and committed to ensure that all decisions involving catastrophe risk, modelled and non-modelled, are based on the latest science, information and analysis, and are carried out in a coherent fashion throughout the organisation.

We are a team that looks out for each other so that we can move forward individually and together through continuous improvement of our work. You will be sharing your technical knowledge and work experience naturally every day with the team and driving your own career development, thus shaping your own and the teams future.

The role

For this role we are looking for someone who can take ownership, work independently, and thrive on ambiguity. The successful candidate will be highly numerate, with an ability to think creatively and communicate effectively. You will need to confidently make sound business decisions and back these up with relevant data. You will need to find solutions to problems where there is not an established approach.

What you will be doing as an Exposure Management Analyst in our team:

Business as usual support


Your priority will be to ensure that the Underwriting Teams are equipped with the latest exposure information and are provided with insights upon the direction of travel of the portfolios exposures. A good amount of time will also be spent on delivering exposure roll-ups to the Hiscox Group to meet internal, Investor and Regulatory requirements. You will be responsible for ensuring that the data, methodologies and assumptions used are correct and up to date and that results have been reviewed by and communicated to the Underwriting team.

Driving change


Through your own drive and working together with highly experienced Underwriters, Pricing Analysts, the Group Exposure Management team and external service providers you will strive to continuously improve our approach to exposure management and be leading implementation of meaningful ways to answers exposure management related questions. In addition there is the need to move the existing processes forward and implement new and better ways of working through a controlled environment so more focus can be put on analysis and delivering insight back to the business.

Requirements

This role is suitable for a high-performing, analytical and enthusiastic individual who can associate themselves with the following:

You have a genuine interest in data, analytics, risk and problem-solving, and are excited by the opportunity to build a career within the insurance industry.Whether you're a recent graduate or have some industry experience, you are intellectually curious and enjoy learning new concepts, technologies and ways of working.You have strong numerical and analytical skills, with the ability to interpret data, identify trends and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.You enjoy working collaboratively with a variety of stakeholders and can build effective working relationships across teams.You are naturally inquisitive and can challenge assumptions by translating analysis into meaningful business insights and answering the "so what?".You are highly organised, able to manage competing priorities and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment where demands can be complex and varied.You have a continuous improvement mindset and are motivated by opportunities to increase your technical expertise, commercial understanding and subject matter knowledge.You are interested in using technology, coding, automation and data-driven thinking to solve business problems.


Our Must-Haves

Educated to degree level in Data Analytics, Geography or a related numerate subject, 2:1 or aboveRecent graduates with a strong technical foundation are encouraged to apply, as are candidates with relevant industry or analytical experience.Experience of, or a demonstrable interest in, coding, data analysis and quantitative problem-solving.Knowledge of at least one of the following: Excel, SQL, Python, R, VBA or similar analytical tools.Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.Fluent written and spoken business English.


Our Nice-to-Haves

Experience using Python, SQL, R or other analytical programming languages.Exposure to insurance, risk management, catastrophe modelling or exposure management.Experience working with large or complex datasets.Tableau Desktop experience.Dataiku experience.


Diversity and flexible working at Hiscox

At Hiscox we care about our people. We hire the best people for the job and we’re committed to diversity and creating a truly inclusive culture, which we believe drives success. We also understand that working life doesn’t always have to be ‘nine to five’ and we support flexible working wherever we can. No promises, but please chat to our resourcing team about the flexibility we could offer for this role.

Work with amazing people and be part of a unique culture

rows.title: Data Scientist I - Product
rows.descriptionText:
Data Scientist I - Product Team

London, UK, Reading, UK

Role Impact: As our Data Scientist I - Product, you'll be a core contributor in our Data Science Product team. The Data Scientist I - Product plays a handson role in exploring, modelling and delivering the data science products that power MarketCast's media and entertainment analytics. Operating at the intersection of quantitative market research and statistical modelling, this position focuses on extracting insight from extremely large datasets, building and validating Bayesian and machine learning models, and maintaining the pipelines that turn those models into reliable client outputs. Bayesian methods are central to how the team quantifies uncertainty, incorporates prior knowledge and models hierarchical audience data, and the data scientist is expected to work confidently within that framework. On a daily basis, the data scientist scopes approaches to typical projects, engineers features that address business problems, and discusses technical aspects of the work with internal teams and clients. By producing robust, well-calibrated models and well-maintained products, this individual directly strengthens the accuracy and repeatability of the organisation's analytics.

We're Looking For

Data Exploration & Extraction - The individual explores and extracts data from multiple sources, including TV viewing, advertising and survey data, and interrogates it to create meaningful insights. This is performed in Python and SQL on our AWS data platform, using pandas and increasingly Polars for large-scale processing. Thorough exploration surfaces data quality issues and opportunities before they reach modelling, protecting downstream products from flawed inputs. Success is defined by insights that are accurate, well documented and directly usable by the product and research teams.

Project Scoping & Approach Definition - The role scopes and defines the analytical approach for the typical projects the Data Science Product team works on. The data scientist translates a business or product requirement into a clear technical plan covering data needs, methods and deliverables, and identifies where a Bayesian formulation is the right choice. Sound scoping keeps projects on time and prevents rework late in delivery. Success is measured by approaches that are agreed upfront and hold through to completion with minimal revision.

Bayesian Modelling - The individual builds, fits and validates Bayesian models such as hierarchical regressions, Bayesian time series and probabilistic audience models using frameworks like PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. This involves specifying sensible priors, checking convergence diagnostics and running posterior predictive checks to assess fit. Bayesian modelling allows the team to quantify uncertainty honestly and combine sparse data with prior knowledge, which is essential for outputs used in commercial

decisions. Success is demonstrated by models that are well calibrated, interpretable and communicated in terms of credible intervals rather than point estimates alone.

Machine Learning Development - The role researches, develops and tests solutions using both supervised and unsupervised learning, including forecasting, segmentation, random forests, gradient boosting and support vector machines. The data scientist maintains broad awareness of the techniques available for each problem type and in-depth knowledge in a couple of areas. This breadth allows the right method to be selected rather than the most familiar one. Success is demonstrated by models that meet

agreed evaluation criteria and are appropriate to the product context.

Feature Engineering & Model Robustness - The individual thinks critically about what features are required to address a client business problem and transforms the data to achieve this. This is executed through feature selection techniques, cross-validation and appropriate evaluation metrics, with vigilance against issues such as data leakage. Robust models protect the credibility of product outputs delivered to high-profile clients. Success is defined by models that senior team members can rely on without extensive re-checking.

Pipeline & Product Maintenance - The role maintains and improves existing machine learning and statistical pipelines, processes and products. The data scientist monitors outputs, fixes defects and implements incremental enhancements in collaboration with the India-based Data Engineering team. Stable pipelines ensure recurring deliverables reach clients on schedule and with consistent quality. Success is measured by reduced pipeline failures and improvements delivered without disrupting production.

Insight Visualisation & Reporting - The individual creates bespoke client reports and data visualisations using Tableau and Python plotting libraries, including clear representation of uncertainty from Bayesian outputs. Model results are converted into insight-led charts that follow brand style guides. Effective visualisation lets researchers and clients act on findings quickly. Success is demonstrated by reports that require little clarification and are reused as templates across projects.

Technical Communication & Collaboration - The role discusses the technical and analytical aspects of the work with clients and with the Market Research, Product and Data Engineering teams across the UK, US and India. The data scientist documents requirements, explains Bayesian and ML methods at an appropriate level of detail and participates in internal knowledge-sharing sessions. Clear communication builds trust in the products and reduces misunderstandings on deliverables. Success is measured by stakeholder confidence in the methodology and effective coordination across time zones.

Qualifications: You'll typically have 2 to 4 years' experience working in data science and will have managed projects independently, even if under a senior lead. We'd expect a bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another highly quantitative field, but we care far more about what you can do than what your degree certificate says. If you came to data science by a different route and can demonstrate the skills, we want to hear from you. A master's in a quantitative social science, business analytics or technical discipline is a plus, as is an equivalent practical academic foundation.

Technically, you'll be genuinely proficient in Python, SQL and pandas. Experience with Polars is a strong plus, as we use it increasingly for largescale processing. You'll have a solid grounding in Bayesian statistics, meaning you're comfortable with priors, posterior inference, MCMC and model checking, and you've built real models in at least one probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. You'll also know your way around advanced machine learning algorithms, feature engineering and selection, evaluation metrics and cross-validation, and you'll have some familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure.

Beyond the technical, you'll be able to understand a business problem, draw conclusions from data and recommend actions. You'll communicate clearly, document your work and collaborate well across teams and time zones. An appreciation of quantitative market research techniques is helpful but not necessary. Experience with TV viewing or advertising data, or the media industry more broadly, isn't a prerequisite, but a genuine interest is. Above all, you'll be curious about data and enjoy building visualisations that clearly articulate insight.

Who We Are

MarketCast measures what moves people. Powered by AI, trained on decades of verified consumer response data, along with proprietary technology, MarketCast is the marketing effectiveness partner for the world's most ambitious brands, connecting emotional resonance to real-world business outcomes across advertising, sponsorships, content, brand health, and advanced analytics. With category-deep expertise spanning sports, entertainment, travel, automotive, and consumer brands, our team of

seasoned industry strategists brings unmatched human intelligence to every engagement, turning complex data into decisive action so brands know exactly what's working, why it's working, and what to do next.

At MarketCast, we don't just accept difference - we embrace it, support it, and thrive on it for the benefit of our global culture and success. MarketCast is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know. Check us out on LinkedIn and at: www.marketcast.com

Our Values

Move The Needle

We turn insight into action and action into impact, acting with urgency and intention at every level, anticipating what's needed, executing with discipline, and driving outcomes that are measured and meaningful.

Client Success is Our Scoreboard

We win when our clients win. Delivering scaled, tech-enabled solutions that drive measurable impact and value to build lasting partnerships.

Grow Every Day

Expertise is earned continuously by investing in our craft, our colleagues, and our company.

Own It

Take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs.

Free movie tickets!29 days annual leave PLUS Bank HolidaysFlextime with core hours between 10am and 3pm2 days’ work from home, per week4% match pension schemeEnhanced maternity payRegular social events in both UK locationsProfessional growth and career development including LinkedIn Learning

rows.title: Senior CRM Executive (Lifecycle)
rows.descriptionText:
Stylish, grounded, uplifting – these values live through everything we do at Boden. Without the collaboration, honesty and friendship between our teams, we wouldn’t be where we are today. We curate a world of beauty that’s ethical, inclusive – and importantly – good fun. We inspire you to live your best life. We are Boden.

Overview

This CRM Executive (Lifecycle) role sits within the CRM team and is responsible for the end‑to‑end operational delivery of lifecycle CRM journeys across email and SMS. These journeys play a critical role in strengthening customer loyalty, improving engagement, and driving long‑term value through timely, relevant, and personalised communications.

The CRM Executive (Lifecycle) owns the build, QA, optimisation, and reporting of always‑on CRM journeys, ensuring they operate reliably at scale while continuously improving through structured test‑and‑learn activity. The role combines hands‑on execution with strong ownership of workflow management, data accuracy, QA rigour, and performance reporting.

This role partners closely with Brand, Creative, Insights, and CRM stakeholders to deliver lifecycle campaigns aligned to customer priorities, while identifying opportunities to improve templates, processes, and journey logic to support scalability and performance.

Location: 3 days per week at our North Acton office, 2 days working from home.

What You Will Do

Deliver high-impact lifecycle journeys that strengthen customer loyalty and improve experience across key moments — onboarding, engagement, retention, and reactivation.Own and prioritise the weekly lifecycle build and optimisation schedule, balancing new journey development, BAU maintenance, and optimisation work in line with agreed priorities.Build and QA lifecycle campaigns within Ometria to a high technical and brand standard, using approved templates, modular components, and best-practice journey structures.Partner with CRM Managers, Brand & Creative, and Insights teams during briefing to ensure lifecycle objectives, audiences, triggers, test hypotheses, and success metrics are clearly defined and accurately translated into journey logic and segmentation.Maintain operational excellence across all lifecycle delivery, consistently achieving high QA pass rates, maintaining clear documentation and checklists, and reducing manual effort and risk through continuous process improvement.Monitor live journey performance and campaign data health, proactively identifying underperformance, deliverability risks, or data issues and escalating with clear recommendations.Produce weekly performance reports and analyse journey results against objectives, surfacing actionable insights, clear test outcomes, and optimisation opportunities, ensuring learnings feed back into future iterations and lifecycle strategy.Support A/B testing setup across messaging, timing, cadence, and content, ensuring tests are correctly implemented, documented, and QA'd.

What We Are Looking For

CRM Executive with hands‑on experience delivering lifecycle or triggered CRM campaigns within an ESP or CRM platform (Ometria experience preferred).Highly detail‑oriented, with a strong track record of delivering accurate, reliable, always‑on CRM activity and high QA standards.Comfortable managing complex journey logic and multiple priorities, balancing BAU delivery with optimisation and improvement work.Collaborative and relationship‑driven, with experience working closely with Brand, Creative, and Insight teams.Data‑literate and insight‑driven, confident interpreting lifecycle performance metrics and test results to drive optimisation.Process‑minded and improvement‑focused, with an interest in scaling lifecycle activity through better templates, automation, and ways of working.Proactive and accountable, with strong ownership over journey performance, data quality, and operational standards.Customer‑focused and commercially aware, motivated by delivering CRM that adds long‑term value for both customers and the business.

Our Behaviours

 At Boden, how we work matters just as much as what we deliver. We keep things simple. We say what we mean, keep each other in the loop, and follow through on what we’ve said we’ll do. We care about doing a good job - and we care about each other. We’re always kind, often honest, and we will push for high standards without making it heavy. We know what we’re good at, we lean on each other when needed, and we show up as a team - taking ownership and getting things done together.

What We Offer

Competitive salary & targeted annual bonus scheme.Generous Boden clothing allowance!30% discount on all current clothing ranges.25 days Holiday annually, plus Bank Holidays.Online Portal with an array of discounts on retail & entertainment.Virtual GP Service for you and your household!Free onsite parking and subsidised café.

We want Boden to be the place everyone wants to work. Friendly, open and tolerant. A best-of-British company with diverse teams, equal opportunities, and fair working and recruitment practices. We believe in hiring the best person for the job whoever they are, helping them thrive in it and celebrating their individuality.

We would like to encourage people from a diverse range of backgrounds to apply for our roles. If you need any reasonable adjustments or additional support during your application process, please do not hesitate to let us know.

rows.title: Data & Reporting Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Data & Reporting AnalystInvestment Team · YOU Asset Management
About usYOU Asset Management is a £6.5bn+ multi-asset investment manager. We are the in-house specialist investment arm of Finli, a fast-growing Financial Planning business with offices all over the UK. We have run our flagship Multi-Asset Blend fund range since 2019, and a model portfolio service since 2004. We build portfolios across Equities, Fixed Income, Absolute Return and Real Assets for a range of client risk profiles.Our approach combines disciplined human judgement with a proprietary quantitative framework built from first principles, spanning analysis, asset allocation, risk management, performance attribution and trade execution. We are a small, collaborative team in which every member is given real responsibility early and is expected to contribute their own views.
The roleFirst and foremost we are looking for someone who cares whether the numbers are right. Every decision the investment team takes, and everything we report to clients, rests on data that has been assembled, checked and presented clearly. We want someone who takes ownership of that, who is not afraid to challenge what they are given and who expects to be challenged in turn.The role sits within the Investment Team and involves working with the data, reporting and trade-support infrastructure that underpins how we run money. In the first year, the focus will be on taking ownership of the team’s core monthly and weekly reporting cycle. Over time, the successful candidate will shape how that infrastructure is built, automated and extended.
Your initial focusYou will learn how we run money from the inside by producing the material the team runs it with. Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:— Investment Committee (IAAC) pack. Compiling the monthly committee pack: market returns, valuations and macro indicators, asset allocation positioning, portfolio performance and risk, attribution and deviation monitoring, manager performance, drift, concentration and liquidity reporting, AUM and trading reports. Taking the minutes and drafting the record of actions and decisions— Monthly factsheets. Producing and checking the monthly factsheets for the Multi-Asset Blend funds and model portfolio ranges— Trading support. Calculating trades and rebalances, preparing dealing instructions, and reconciling executed trades and post-trade positions— Ad hoc reporting and analysis. Responding to requests from the investment team, the wider business and clients, from performance queries to bespoke analysis— AI utilisation and automation. Identifying where the reporting cycle is slow, fragile or manual, and fixing it, using AI tools such as Claude alongside conventional automation to remove manual work and raise the quality of what we produce
As you developAs you gain command of the reporting cycle, your focus will shift from producing outputs to owning and improving the infrastructure behind them:— Quantitative framework. Helping to build, maintain and extend the team’s analytical, risk, attribution and trading tools— Data infrastructure. Designing the data pipelines that feed our reporting, so that outputs are reproducible and reconciled by construction rather than by hand— Trading and execution analysis. Deepening our trading cost analysis and best execution monitoring— Team development. Documenting processes and helping analysts across the team get the most out of the tools
Who we are looking forWe value how a candidate thinks, and how they work with others, above any particular background. Character and attitude matter to us as much as technical ability, and the following qualities matter most:— Rigour and attention to detail. Meticulous in checking your own work, constructive in reviewing others’, and healthily sceptical of any number until you understand where it came from— Ownership and reliability. The reporting cycle has hard deadlines. Committee packs, factsheets and trade instructions have to be right and on time, every month— A problem-solving instinct. Inclined to fix a broken process rather than work around it, and to propose solutions rather than simply highlight problems— Independent, evidence-led thinking. Comfortable telling a fund manager that a figure is wrong, and able to explain why— Intellectual honesty. Willing to flag your own errors quickly, and to change your approach when the evidence changes— Clear reasoning and communication. Able to capture a committee debate faithfully in minutes, and to present data so that a fund manager, a compliance officer or a financial adviser can read it without further explanation— Curiosity and range. A genuine interest in markets and in how a multi-asset portfolio is put together— Collaboration. Generous with what you know, open to feedback, and invested in the success of the team as a whole, not only your own work
Credentials and skills— Academic background. A strong degree in a quantitative or analytical discipline such as mathematics, statistics, economics, finance, engineering, computer science or the sciences. An investment background is welcome but not required— Technical fluency. Strong Excel is essential. Fluency with Python, VBA, Claude and market data platforms such as Refinitiv Datastream and FE Analytics is expected to be gained very rapidly if not already held. Experience with SQL, PowerPoint automation or performance attribution is an advantage— Qualifications. The Investment Management Certificate (IMC), or a commitment to attain it promptly— Eligibility. The right to work in the UK— Location. This is a London-based role, at our offices in Cheapside

rows.title: Market Intelligence & Research Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
KPay Group (“KPay”) is a leading fintech company committed to empowering businesses of all sizes through simple, seamless, smart and secure technology solutions. Serving more than 95,000 merchants across Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, and Singapore, KPay helps unlock growth potential by building a one-stop platform for financial management, business operations, and digital transformation.
In 2024, KPay raised a record-breaking USD 55 million in its Series A funding round — the largest globally in the payments sector that year. The company has since been recognised as PayTech of the Year at the 2025 Asia FinTech Awards, selected on Forbes Asia’s 100 to Watch list in 2025, and ranked among Singapore's Top FinTech Companies 2026, curated by Tech in Asia and Statista.
About the RoleWe’re looking for a Market Intelligence & Research Analyst to support KPay’s UK and wider Europe market entry through in-depth market research, competitive intelligence, and data-driven analysis. As one of the early members of KPay’s UK expansion team, you’ll play a key role in understanding the UK payments landscape, identifying high-potential merchant segments and regions, and uncovering opportunities for commercial growth.
You’ll research UK merchants, competitors, industry trends, product offerings, pricing structures, and market positioning to understand customer needs and competitive dynamics. Beyond desk research, you’ll validate assumptions through data analysis and merchant interviews, translating findings into clear, actionable recommendations on where to focus, how to position our offerings, and how to approach market expansion.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys investigating markets, connecting insights across different sources, and turning research into practical business recommendations. You’ll have the opportunity to shape KPay’s UK expansion strategy from the ground up in a fast-paced, 0-to-1 environment where your findings will directly inform commercial decisions.
ResponsibilitiesUK Market & Regional Research: Conduct in-depth research into the UK payments landscape, assessing market size, regional opportunities, merchant demographics, industry trends, and growth potential across different locations and verticals.Competitive Intelligence: Analyse competitor products, pricing, fee structures, value propositions, distribution channels, and market positioning to identify competitive gaps and differentiation opportunities.Merchant Research & Customer Insights: Research UK SME needs, payment behaviours, operational challenges, and purchasing considerations. Conduct merchant interviews and gather first-hand insights to validate market assumptions.Market Opportunity Assessment: Evaluate potential merchant segments, industry verticals, and geographic markets using quantitative and qualitative data to identify and prioritise opportunities for expansion.Data Analysis & Hypothesis Validation: Gather, clean, and analyse market and competitor data to test assumptions, identify patterns, and support evidence-based decision-making.Strategic Recommendations: Translate research findings into clear recommendations on target markets, customer segments, competitive positioning, product offerings, pricing considerations, and market entry approaches.Market Intelligence Reporting: Develop structured research reports, competitor benchmarking, market maps, and insight dashboards to support the Regional team’s planning and decision-making.GTM Strategy Support: Collaborate with Strategy, Finance, Product, Marketing, and Commercial teams to ensure market insights inform go-to-market strategies, product positioning, and expansion initiatives.Ongoing Market Monitoring: Track changes in competitor activity, industry developments, regulatory considerations, and market trends to identify emerging opportunities and risks.
RequirementsMinimum 1 year of relevant experience in market research, strategy, consulting, business intelligence, commercial analysis, or a related field; fresh graduates with strong analytical and research backgrounds are welcome to apply too.Strong research skills, with the ability to independently investigate unfamiliar markets and products, identify relevant information, and draw meaningful conclusions.Strong analytical capabilities, with experience collecting, interpreting, and synthesising quantitative and qualitative data.Excellent critical thinking skills, with the ability to challenge assumptions, assess the reliability of information, and validate hypotheses using evidence.Strong commercial awareness and an interest in fintech, payments, the UK SME landscape, and competitive market dynamics.Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint for data analysis and presenting findings; experience with SQL, data visualisation tools, or web data crawling is a plus.Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex research into concise, structured, and actionable recommendations.Detail-oriented, resourceful, and self-driven, with the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment where processes are still being developed.Comfortable with ambiguity and excited by the opportunity to contribute to building a new market from 0 to 1.Based in the UK; right to work required.

We’re the world’s leading sports technology company, at the intersection between sports, media, and betting. More than 1,700 sports federations, media outlets, betting operators, and consumer platforms across 120 countries rely on our know-how and technology to boost their business.



Job Description

OVERVIEW

Make the team that changes the way the world experiences sport.

Sportradar is the leading global provider of sports betting and sports entertainment products and services. Since 2001, we have occupied a unique position at the intersection of the sports, media and betting industries, providing sports federations, news media, consumer platforms and sports betting operators with a range of solutions to help grow their business.

The Operational Account Management (OAM) team acts as the main point of contact between our growing client base and Sportradar. We are looking for a dedicated Business Intelligence Analyst to support the unit by developing interactive analytical applications, scheduled customer reports and ad hoc customer report requests. The Business Intelligence Analyst will also recommend and implement improvements to our reporting processes that allow us to automate specific requests coming from our client base.

THE CHALLENGE

Deliver state-of-the-art data analytics and reporting solutions leveraging our data.Development of data visualisations and reports for analysing datasets (Power BI, Excel).Periodic reporting: automatic setup and distribution of reports.Present ideas and solutions to business users and software developers in a clear and understandable way.Propose new, innovative ways of using data to improve our products and services.Participate in data modelling for reporting and analytics.Co-create and deliver an ambitious business intelligence roadmap in close coordination with various business and technical stakeholders across Sportradar.YOUR PROFILE

Demonstrated technical expertise in business intelligence tools, the design and development of data analytics solutions and reports, and querying databases with SQL.Solid hands-on SQL skills — writing and optimising queries, joins and aggregations against large datasets.Prior experience working on projects related to data management and/or business intelligence.The successful candidate will be practised in hands-on development of software or analytics solutions. Knowledge of VBA beneficial.Experience with Power BI (data modelling, DAX, Power Query) is a benefit — as is experience with comparable BI platforms, since we're happy to support the transition.Knowledge of data governance practices and Power BI security — workspace access, row-level security and controlled sharing of client data — is a benefit.An understanding of the gaming and sports betting industry is a strong advantage.Experience working with Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena and/or Microsoft SQL Server is a benefit.OUR OFFER:

A collaborative environment with colleagues from all over the world (Engineering offices in Europe, Asia and US) including various social events and teambuilding. Flexibility to manage your workday and tasks with autonomy. A balance of structure and autonomy to tackle your daily tasks. Vibrant and inclusive community, including Women in Tech and Pride groups which welcome all participants. Global Employee Assistance Programme. Calm and Reulay app (leading well-being apps designed to support focus, quality rest, mindfulness, and long-term mental resilience). Online training videos. Flexible working hours.  

While we appreciate the flexibility and benefits of working from home, we strongly believe that coming together in person fosters stronger connections, encourages collaboration, and drives innovation—both as individuals and as a company. The energy, shared ideas, and team support we experience in the office strengthen the foundation of our success and culture. For this reason, we are an office-first business operating on a fully on-site model, with team members working in the office four days a week to build relationships, exchange ideas, and grow together. Certain exemptions may apply depending on location — your local point of contact can provide further details. 



Additional Information

At Sportradar, we celebrate our diverse group of hardworking employees. Sportradar is committed to ensuring equal access to its programs, facilities, and employment opportunities. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. We encourage you to apply even if you only meet most of the requirements (but not 100% of the listed criteria) – we believe skills evolve over time. If you’re willing to learn and grow with us, we invite you to join our team!

rows.title: Global FP&A Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
Music is Universal

It’s the passionate and dedicated team at Universal Music who help make us the world’s leading music company. From A&R to finance, legal to digital, sales to marketing, Universal Music is the place to grow and develop your career within a truly commercial and innovative business that leads in everything it does.

Everyone is welcome to apply for our roles, and we are determined to ensure that no applicant or employee receives less favourable treatment because of gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion, belief, age, marital status, background, pregnancy, or caring responsibilities. We also recognise the importance of diversity of thought within our teams and are fully committed to embracing the talents of people with autism, dyslexia, ADHD, and other forms of neurocognitive variation.

We will always seek to make appropriate adjustments to recruitment, workplaces, and work processes to be fully inclusive to people with different needs and working styles. If you need us to make any reasonable adjustments for you from application onwards, including alternatives to the online form or to disclose a neurocognitive condition, please email UniversalMusicCareers@umusic.com.

The Department/Role 

The Global Finance FP&A team is responsible for the review and analysis of UMG’s financial performance at a global, divisional and operating company level, communicating the results and key insights to management through financial reports, analysis and presentations.

The team closely supports the UMG CFO, Group Controller, UMG Board and Investor Relations teams, and works closely with Heads of Finance across the operating companies.

The Group FP&A Analyst, reporting to the Global FP&A Manager, will play a key role in the review and analysis of UMG’s consolidated global results, including revenue, profitability and cash flow performance. The role will also take responsibility for a portfolio of territories, developing a strong understanding of their businesses and acting as a key point of contact within Global Finance for their financial performance, forecasts and other finance-related matters.

Key Responsibilities

Take primary FP&A responsibility for a portfolio of territories, acting as the Global Finance point of contact and working closely with local Finance teams to review and understand financial performance, forecasts and key business drivers. Perform detailed variance analysis and investigations of actual and forecast results against budget, prior forecasts and other relevant benchmarks, identifying and explaining key performance drivers, trends, risks and opportunities across Group, divisional and operating company levels. Review and analyse cash flow performance and forecasts, including investigation of material variances and identification of the principal drivers of cash generation and working capital performance. Prepare and analyse key monthly financial reports covering Group, divisional and operating company performance, ensuring that significant movements, trends and business drivers are clearly understood and communicated. Support the preparation of financial analysis and presentations for the UMG CFO, Group Controller, UMG Board and other senior management, ensuring that key financial messages and business drivers are communicated clearly and accurately. Support the Group forecasting, budgeting and longer-term planning processes, including review and challenge of operating company submissions and consolidation and analysis of Group results. Support adherence to UMG accounting policies and relevant IFRS requirements, working closely with the Group Financial Reporting team and operating company Finance teams as appropriate. Provide additional ad hoc financial analysis support to the UMG CFO, Group Controller and Global Finance EVP as well as other senior stakeholders. 

Must Have

Skills and Experience Required

A recognised professional accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent). Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex financial information, identify key performance drivers and draw clear, commercially relevant conclusions. Financial modelling and advanced Excel skills, with experience of building and maintaining robust financial models and analytical tools. Experience with macros and/or other automation tools would be advantageous. Ability to explain and present financial results, key trends and complex issues in a clear, accurate and concise manner to both finance and non-finance stakeholders. Strong interpersonal and business-partnering skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with colleagues across different territories, functions and levels of seniority. Attention to detail, with the ability to interpret financial information in the broader commercial context and identify key business drivers. Ability to manage competing priorities, take ownership of deliverables and work effectively to tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Collaborative approach and strong work ethic, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a wider team. Proactive and improvement-focused mindset, with the ability to add value through enhanced analysis, development and continuous improvements of processes and reporting. An interest in music and enthusiasm for working within the music and entertainment industry. 

Nice To Have

Experience working within a large, complex multinational organisation and/or a multi-territory finance environment. Experience with Hyperion or similar enterprise performance management, consolidation and reporting systems. 

Just So You Know…

The company presents this job description as a guide to the major areas and duties for which the jobholder is accountable. However, the business operates in an environment that demands change and the jobholder's specific responsibilities and activities will vary and develop. Therefore, the job description should be seen as indicative and not as a permanent, definitive, and exhaustive statement.

rows.title: Commercial Planning Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
At Too Good To Go, we have an ambitious mission: to inspire and empower everyone to fight food waste together.

More than 1/3 of all food produced in the world is wasted. And that has a huge impact on the health of our planet. 10% of greenhouse gas emissions come from food waste and loss.

Through our marketplace app, we connect businesses that have unsold, surplus food, with consumers who can buy and enjoy it at ⅓ of retail value. We are a certified B Corporation with a mission to empower everyone to take action against food waste. Alongside our marketplace app, we create educational tools, explore new business solutions, and influence legislation to help reduce food waste.

We’re growing fast: Our community of 120 million registered users and 180,000 active partners across 20 countries, have together already saved over 500 million meals from going to waste

In 2023, Too Good To Go was recognised on Fortune's acclaimed 'Change the World' list, named as one of Deloitte's 'Best Managed Companies' and won a coveted 'Cultural Impact Award' at the annual Apple App Store Awards.

About The Role

This role will report to the Commercial Planning Manager and support commercial planning, forecasting, latest estimates, statistical analysis and performance modelling. You'll help develop the analytical insight that underpins commercial decisions by combining business understanding with statistical techniques, causal analysis and AI-assisted workflows. You’ll help make sure the team has the right data, reporting and analysis needed to understand business performance and make better decisions.

The Commercial Planning Manager will own the overall planning rhythm, including budgeting, 4+8 forecasting, monthly latest estimates and commercial deep dives. Your role will be to support that process by preparing analysis, maintaining key reporting outputs, investigating performance movements and helping turn data into clear insight.

The Parcels business moves quickly, with many variables across countries, items, partners, parcel types, pricing, demand and inventory. We need someone who enjoys investigating why performance changes, is naturally curious about causal relationships rather than simply reporting numbers, and is interested in applying statistical techniques and modern AI tools to improve analysis and forecasting.

This is a great role for someone who is already strong in commercial analysis, confident working with data, and able to quickly understand a fast-moving business. You’ll need to bring structure, accuracy and sharp analytical thinking from day one, helping the Commercial Planning Manager and wider Planning team make better decisions.

What You’ll Do

The Department/Role 

The Global Finance FP&A team is responsible for the review and analysis of UMG’s financial performance at a global, divisional and operating company level, communicating the results and key insights to management through financial reports, analysis and presentations.

The team closely supports the UMG CFO, Group Controller, UMG Board and Investor Relations teams, and works closely with Heads of Finance across the operating companies.

The Group FP&A Analyst, reporting to the Global FP&A Manager, will play a key role in the review and analysis of UMG’s consolidated global results, including revenue, profitability and cash flow performance. The role will also take responsibility for a portfolio of territories, developing a strong understanding of their businesses and acting as a key point of contact within Global Finance for their financial performance, forecasts and other finance-related matters.

Key Responsibilities

Take primary FP&A responsibility for a portfolio of territories, acting as the Global Finance point of contact and working closely with local Finance teams to review and understand financial performance, forecasts and key business drivers. Perform detailed variance analysis and investigations of actual and forecast results against budget, prior forecasts and other relevant benchmarks, identifying and explaining key performance drivers, trends, risks and opportunities across Group, divisional and operating company levels. Review and analyse cash flow performance and forecasts, including investigation of material variances and identification of the principal drivers of cash generation and working capital performance. Prepare and analyse key monthly financial reports covering Group, divisional and operating company performance, ensuring that significant movements, trends and business drivers are clearly understood and communicated. Support the preparation of financial analysis and presentations for the UMG CFO, Group Controller, UMG Board and other senior management, ensuring that key financial messages and business drivers are communicated clearly and accurately. Support the Group forecasting, budgeting and longer-term planning processes, including review and challenge of operating company submissions and consolidation and analysis of Group results. Support adherence to UMG accounting policies and relevant IFRS requirements, working closely with the Group Financial Reporting team and operating company Finance teams as appropriate. Provide additional ad hoc financial analysis support to the UMG CFO, Group Controller and Global Finance EVP as well as other senior stakeholders. 

Must Have

Skills and Experience Required

A recognised professional accounting qualification (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent). Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to interpret complex financial information, identify key performance drivers and draw clear, commercially relevant conclusions. Financial modelling and advanced Excel skills, with experience of building and maintaining robust financial models and analytical tools. Experience with macros and/or other automation tools would be advantageous. Ability to explain and present financial results, key trends and complex issues in a clear, accurate and concise manner to both finance and non-finance stakeholders. Strong interpersonal and business-partnering skills, with the ability to build effective relationships with colleagues across different territories, functions and levels of seniority. Attention to detail, with the ability to interpret financial information in the broader commercial context and identify key business drivers. Ability to manage competing priorities, take ownership of deliverables and work effectively to tight deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Collaborative approach and strong work ethic, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a wider team. Proactive and improvement-focused mindset, with the ability to add value through enhanced analysis, development and continuous improvements of processes and reporting. An interest in music and enthusiasm for working within the music and entertainment industry. 

Nice To Have

Experience working within a large, complex multinational organisation and/or a multi-territory finance environment. Experience with Hyperion or similar enterprise performance management, consolidation and reporting systems. 

Just So You Know…

The company presents this job description as a guide to the major areas and duties for which the jobholder is accountable. However, the business operates in an environment that demands change and the jobholder's specific responsibilities and activities will vary and develop. Therefore, the job description should be seen as indicative and not as a permanent, definitive, and exhaustive statement.

Data Scientist I - Product Team

London, UK, Reading, UK

Role Impact: As our Data Scientist I - Product, you'll be a core contributor in our Data Science Product team. The Data Scientist I - Product plays a handson role in exploring, modelling and delivering the data science products that power MarketCast's media and entertainment analytics. Operating at the intersection of quantitative market research and statistical modelling, this position focuses on extracting insight from extremely large datasets, building and validating Bayesian and machine learning models, and maintaining the pipelines that turn those models into reliable client outputs. Bayesian methods are central to how the team quantifies uncertainty, incorporates prior knowledge and models hierarchical audience data, and the data scientist is expected to work confidently within that framework. On a daily basis, the data scientist scopes approaches to typical projects, engineers features that address business problems, and discusses technical aspects of the work with internal teams and clients. By producing robust, well-calibrated models and well-maintained products, this individual directly strengthens the accuracy and repeatability of the organisation's analytics.

We're Looking For

Data Exploration & Extraction - The individual explores and extracts data from multiple sources, including TV viewing, advertising and survey data, and interrogates it to create meaningful insights. This is performed in Python and SQL on our AWS data platform, using pandas and increasingly Polars for large-scale processing. Thorough exploration surfaces data quality issues and opportunities before they reach modelling, protecting downstream products from flawed inputs. Success is defined by insights that are accurate, well documented and directly usable by the product and research teams.

Project Scoping & Approach Definition - The role scopes and defines the analytical approach for the typical projects the Data Science Product team works on. The data scientist translates a business or product requirement into a clear technical plan covering data needs, methods and deliverables, and identifies where a Bayesian formulation is the right choice. Sound scoping keeps projects on time and prevents rework late in delivery. Success is measured by approaches that are agreed upfront and hold through to completion with minimal revision.

Bayesian Modelling - The individual builds, fits and validates Bayesian models such as hierarchical regressions, Bayesian time series and probabilistic audience models using frameworks like PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. This involves specifying sensible priors, checking convergence diagnostics and running posterior predictive checks to assess fit. Bayesian modelling allows the team to quantify uncertainty honestly and combine sparse data with prior knowledge, which is essential for outputs used in commercial

decisions. Success is demonstrated by models that are well calibrated, interpretable and communicated in terms of credible intervals rather than point estimates alone.

Machine Learning Development - The role researches, develops and tests solutions using both supervised and unsupervised learning, including forecasting, segmentation, random forests, gradient boosting and support vector machines. The data scientist maintains broad awareness of the techniques available for each problem type and in-depth knowledge in a couple of areas. This breadth allows the right method to be selected rather than the most familiar one. Success is demonstrated by models that meet

agreed evaluation criteria and are appropriate to the product context.

Feature Engineering & Model Robustness - The individual thinks critically about what features are required to address a client business problem and transforms the data to achieve this. This is executed through feature selection techniques, cross-validation and appropriate evaluation metrics, with vigilance against issues such as data leakage. Robust models protect the credibility of product outputs delivered to high-profile clients. Success is defined by models that senior team members can rely on without extensive re-checking.

Pipeline & Product Maintenance - The role maintains and improves existing machine learning and statistical pipelines, processes and products. The data scientist monitors outputs, fixes defects and implements incremental enhancements in collaboration with the India-based Data Engineering team. Stable pipelines ensure recurring deliverables reach clients on schedule and with consistent quality. Success is measured by reduced pipeline failures and improvements delivered without disrupting production.

Insight Visualisation & Reporting - The individual creates bespoke client reports and data visualisations using Tableau and Python plotting libraries, including clear representation of uncertainty from Bayesian outputs. Model results are converted into insight-led charts that follow brand style guides. Effective visualisation lets researchers and clients act on findings quickly. Success is demonstrated by reports that require little clarification and are reused as templates across projects.

Technical Communication & Collaboration - The role discusses the technical and analytical aspects of the work with clients and with the Market Research, Product and Data Engineering teams across the UK, US and India. The data scientist documents requirements, explains Bayesian and ML methods at an appropriate level of detail and participates in internal knowledge-sharing sessions. Clear communication builds trust in the products and reduces misunderstandings on deliverables. Success is measured by stakeholder confidence in the methodology and effective coordination across time zones.

Qualifications: You'll typically have 2 to 4 years' experience working in data science and will have managed projects independently, even if under a senior lead. We'd expect a bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another highly quantitative field, but we care far more about what you can do than what your degree certificate says. If you came to data science by a different route and can demonstrate the skills, we want to hear from you. A master's in a quantitative social science, business analytics or technical discipline is a plus, as is an equivalent practical academic foundation.

Technically, you'll be genuinely proficient in Python, SQL and pandas. Experience with Polars is a strong plus, as we use it increasingly for largescale processing. You'll have a solid grounding in Bayesian statistics, meaning you're comfortable with priors, posterior inference, MCMC and model checking, and you've built real models in at least one probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. You'll also know your way around advanced machine learning algorithms, feature engineering and selection, evaluation metrics and cross-validation, and you'll have some familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure.

Beyond the technical, you'll be able to understand a business problem, draw conclusions from data and recommend actions. You'll communicate clearly, document your work and collaborate well across teams and time zones. An appreciation of quantitative market research techniques is helpful but not necessary. Experience with TV viewing or advertising data, or the media industry more broadly, isn't a prerequisite, but a genuine interest is. Above all, you'll be curious about data and enjoy building visualisations that clearly articulate insight.

Who We Are

MarketCast measures what moves people. Powered by AI, trained on decades of verified consumer response data, along with proprietary technology, MarketCast is the marketing effectiveness partner for the world's most ambitious brands, connecting emotional resonance to real-world business outcomes across advertising, sponsorships, content, brand health, and advanced analytics. With category-deep expertise spanning sports, entertainment, travel, automotive, and consumer brands, our team of

seasoned industry strategists brings unmatched human intelligence to every engagement, turning complex data into decisive action so brands know exactly what's working, why it's working, and what to do next.

Our Values

We turn insight into action and action into impact, acting with urgency and intention at every level, anticipating what's needed, executing with discipline, and driving outcomes that are measured and meaningful.

Client Success is Our Scoreboard

We win when our clients win. Delivering scaled, tech-enabled solutions that drive measurable impact and value to build lasting partnerships.

rows.title: Data Scientist I - Product
rows.descriptionText:
Data Scientist I - Product Team

London, UK, Reading, UK

Role Impact: As our Data Scientist I - Product, you'll be a core contributor in our Data Science Product team. The Data Scientist I - Product plays a handson role in exploring, modelling and delivering the data science products that power MarketCast's media and entertainment analytics. Operating at the intersection of quantitative market research and statistical modelling, this position focuses on extracting insight from extremely large datasets, building and validating Bayesian and machine learning models, and maintaining the pipelines that turn those models into reliable client outputs. Bayesian methods are central to how the team quantifies uncertainty, incorporates prior knowledge and models hierarchical audience data, and the data scientist is expected to work confidently within that framework. On a daily basis, the data scientist scopes approaches to typical projects, engineers features that address business problems, and discusses technical aspects of the work with internal teams and clients. By producing robust, well-calibrated models and well-maintained products, this individual directly strengthens the accuracy and repeatability of the organisation's analytics.

We're Looking For

Data Exploration & Extraction - The individual explores and extracts data from multiple sources, including TV viewing, advertising and survey data, and interrogates it to create meaningful insights. This is performed in Python and SQL on our AWS data platform, using pandas and increasingly Polars for large-scale processing. Thorough exploration surfaces data quality issues and opportunities before they reach modelling, protecting downstream products from flawed inputs. Success is defined by insights that are accurate, well documented and directly usable by the product and research teams.

Project Scoping & Approach Definition - The role scopes and defines the analytical approach for the typical projects the Data Science Product team works on. The data scientist translates a business or product requirement into a clear technical plan covering data needs, methods and deliverables, and identifies where a Bayesian formulation is the right choice. Sound scoping keeps projects on time and prevents rework late in delivery. Success is measured by approaches that are agreed upfront and hold through to completion with minimal revision.

Bayesian Modelling - The individual builds, fits and validates Bayesian models such as hierarchical regressions, Bayesian time series and probabilistic audience models using frameworks like PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. This involves specifying sensible priors, checking convergence diagnostics and running posterior predictive checks to assess fit. Bayesian modelling allows the team to quantify uncertainty honestly and combine sparse data with prior knowledge, which is essential for outputs used in commercial

decisions. Success is demonstrated by models that are well calibrated, interpretable and communicated in terms of credible intervals rather than point estimates alone.

Machine Learning Development - The role researches, develops and tests solutions using both supervised and unsupervised learning, including forecasting, segmentation, random forests, gradient boosting and support vector machines. The data scientist maintains broad awareness of the techniques available for each problem type and in-depth knowledge in a couple of areas. This breadth allows the right method to be selected rather than the most familiar one. Success is demonstrated by models that meet

agreed evaluation criteria and are appropriate to the product context.

Feature Engineering & Model Robustness - The individual thinks critically about what features are required to address a client business problem and transforms the data to achieve this. This is executed through feature selection techniques, cross-validation and appropriate evaluation metrics, with vigilance against issues such as data leakage. Robust models protect the credibility of product outputs delivered to high-profile clients. Success is defined by models that senior team members can rely on without extensive re-checking.

Pipeline & Product Maintenance - The role maintains and improves existing machine learning and statistical pipelines, processes and products. The data scientist monitors outputs, fixes defects and implements incremental enhancements in collaboration with the India-based Data Engineering team. Stable pipelines ensure recurring deliverables reach clients on schedule and with consistent quality. Success is measured by reduced pipeline failures and improvements delivered without disrupting production.

Insight Visualisation & Reporting - The individual creates bespoke client reports and data visualisations using Tableau and Python plotting libraries, including clear representation of uncertainty from Bayesian outputs. Model results are converted into insight-led charts that follow brand style guides. Effective visualisation lets researchers and clients act on findings quickly. Success is demonstrated by reports that require little clarification and are reused as templates across projects.

Technical Communication & Collaboration - The role discusses the technical and analytical aspects of the work with clients and with the Market Research, Product and Data Engineering teams across the UK, US and India. The data scientist documents requirements, explains Bayesian and ML methods at an appropriate level of detail and participates in internal knowledge-sharing sessions. Clear communication builds trust in the products and reduces misunderstandings on deliverables. Success is measured by stakeholder confidence in the methodology and effective coordination across time zones.

Qualifications: You'll typically have 2 to 4 years' experience working in data science and will have managed projects independently, even if under a senior lead. We'd expect a bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or another highly quantitative field, but we care far more about what you can do than what your degree certificate says. If you came to data science by a different route and can demonstrate the skills, we want to hear from you. A master's in a quantitative social science, business analytics or technical discipline is a plus, as is an equivalent practical academic foundation.

Technically, you'll be genuinely proficient in Python, SQL and pandas. Experience with Polars is a strong plus, as we use it increasingly for largescale processing. You'll have a solid grounding in Bayesian statistics, meaning you're comfortable with priors, posterior inference, MCMC and model checking, and you've built real models in at least one probabilistic programming framework such as PyMC, Stan or NumPyro. You'll also know your way around advanced machine learning algorithms, feature engineering and selection, evaluation metrics and cross-validation, and you'll have some familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure.

Beyond the technical, you'll be able to understand a business problem, draw conclusions from data and recommend actions. You'll communicate clearly, document your work and collaborate well across teams and time zones. An appreciation of quantitative market research techniques is helpful but not necessary. Experience with TV viewing or advertising data, or the media industry more broadly, isn't a prerequisite, but a genuine interest is. Above all, you'll be curious about data and enjoy building visualisations that clearly articulate insight.

Who We Are

MarketCast measures what moves people. Powered by AI, trained on decades of verified consumer response data, along with proprietary technology, MarketCast is the marketing effectiveness partner for the world's most ambitious brands, connecting emotional resonance to real-world business outcomes across advertising, sponsorships, content, brand health, and advanced analytics. With category-deep expertise spanning sports, entertainment, travel, automotive, and consumer brands, our team of

seasoned industry strategists brings unmatched human intelligence to every engagement, turning complex data into decisive action so brands know exactly what's working, why it's working, and what to do next.

At MarketCast, we don't just accept difference - we embrace it, support it, and thrive on it for the benefit of our global culture and success. MarketCast is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. We also consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know. Check us out on LinkedIn and at: www.marketcast.com

Our Values

Move The Needle

We turn insight into action and action into impact, acting with urgency and intention at every level, anticipating what's needed, executing with discipline, and driving outcomes that are measured and meaningful.

Client Success is Our Scoreboard

We win when our clients win. Delivering scaled, tech-enabled solutions that drive measurable impact and value to build lasting partnerships.

Grow Every Day

Expertise is earned continuously by investing in our craft, our colleagues, and our company.

Own It

Take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs.

Free movie tickets!29 days annual leave PLUS Bank HolidaysFlextime with core hours between 10am and 3pm2 days’ work from home, per week4% match pension schemeEnhanced maternity payRegular social events in both UK locationsProfessional growth and career development including LinkedIn Learning

The Operational Account Management (OAM) team acts as the main point of contact between our growing client base and Sportradar. We are looking for a dedicated Business Intelligence Analyst to support the unit by developing interactive analytical applications, scheduled customer reports and ad hoc customer report requests. The Business Intelligence Analyst will also recommend and implement improvements to our reporting processes that allow us to automate specific requests coming from our client base.

THE CHALLENGE

Deliver state-of-the-art data analytics and reporting solutions leveraging our data.Development of data visualisations and reports for analysing datasets (Power BI, Excel).Periodic reporting: automatic setup and distribution of reports.Present ideas and solutions to business users and software developers in a clear and understandable way.Propose new, innovative ways of using data to improve our products and services.Participate in data modelling for reporting and analytics.Co-create and deliver an ambitious business intelligence roadmap in close coordination with various business and technical stakeholders across Sportradar.YOUR PROFILE

Demonstrated technical expertise in business intelligence tools, the design and development of data analytics solutions and reports, and querying databases with SQL.Solid hands-on SQL skills — writing and optimising queries, joins and aggregations against large datasets.Prior experience working on projects related to data management and/or business intelligence.The successful candidate will be practised in hands-on development of software or analytics solutions. Knowledge of VBA beneficial.Experience with Power BI (data modelling, DAX, Power Query) is a benefit — as is experience with comparable BI platforms, since we're happy to support the transition.Knowledge of data governance practices and Power BI security — workspace access, row-level security and controlled sharing of client data — is a benefit.An understanding of the gaming and sports betting industry is a strong advantage.Experience working with Amazon Redshift, Amazon Athena and/or Microsoft SQL Server is a benefit.OUR OFFER:
