rows.descriptionText:
DIVISION: BPS Operations

OFFICE: Transportation Department

TEAM: Data & Strategy

ACADEMIC/NON-ACADEMIC: NON-ACADEMIC

____________________________________________________________________________________

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

rows.descriptionText:
Job Title: Data AnalystTerm: Through February 2027 (can extend)Location: Wilmington MA then Andover, MASchedule: On-Site 5 Days/Week
Position Summary The Quality Data Analyst / Administrator supports the Quality organization by managing quality-related data, customer field issue records, corrective action tracking, return material activity, and reporting for manufacturing and field quality processes. This role helps ensure accurate, timely, and audit-ready information across systems such as AssurX, Excel, Power BI, SharePoint, and related business tools.
Key Responsibilities Customer Field Issue and AssurX Administration: Manage records for OBQ, failure analysis, DOA, field RMA, and related customer quality issues. Maintain accurate case status, ownership, due dates, supporting documentation, and escalation visibility.Quality Data Reporting: Develop and maintain quality trend reports, dashboards, and summaries for Quality Engineering, Supplier Quality Engineering, Technical Support, Product Management, Logistics, and leadership using Excel, Power BI, and other reporting tools.Returned Material and Failure Analysis Coordination: Track returned parts, field RMA activity, supplier FA requests, routing concerns, and return-to-vendor instructions. Coordinate with Logistics, Engineering, Factory teams, suppliers, and field service teams to maintain timely closure.CAPA / 8D Coordination: Support corrective action processes by tracking 8D progress, action owners, due dates, containment, root cause investigation status, corrective action implementation, and effectiveness verification.Procedure, Part, and Disposition Follow-Up: Follow up with responsible departments on procedure revisions, part disposition decisions, engineering updates, SOP changes, and release status tied to quality investigations.Field Service and Stock Purge Support: Coordinate field service corrective action upgrades, stock purges, and material disposition activities with Logistics and responsible functional teams.ISO 9001 and Audit Support: Support ISO 9001 quality system activities, maintain audit-ready records, and train toward qualification as an internal ISO 9001 auditor.Product Change Notice Support: Support LBU Product Change Notice application processing, including data review, routing, follow-up, and status tracking.
Required Qualifications Associate degree, technical degree, or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience required; bachelor’s degree in Quality, Engineering, Data Analytics, Business, or a related field preferred.2–5 years of organizational, administrative, data management, quality, manufacturing, RMA, MRB, or transaction-processing experience in a manufacturing or technical environment.Intermediate to advanced Microsoft Excel skills required, including data cleanup, filtering, pivot tables, formulas, and structured tracking files.MS Office Apps, PowerBI required, AI/Copilot a plusStrong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare concise updates, status summaries, and PowerPoint presentations.Ability to coordinate multiple open actions, follow up across functions, maintain accurate records, and escalate issues when needed.Experience with RMA, MRB, CAPA, 8D, supplier failure analysis, ISO 9001, or quality system documentation is a plus.
Preferred Skills and Competencies High attention to detail and strong ownership of data accuracy.Ability to translate quality case activity into meaningful metrics, trends, and management summaries.Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.Comfort working with cross-functional teams, including Engineering, Quality, Supplier Quality, Product Management, Logistics, Field Service, Manufacturing, and suppliers.Continuous improvement mindset and willingness to standardize workflows, templates, and reporting methods.
Success Measures Accurate and timely maintenance of customer quality issue records.Improved visibility to OBQ, DOA, FA, RMA, CAPA, and 8D status.Reduced overdue action items through consistent follow-up and escalation.Reliable trend reporting that supports management review and corrective action prioritization.Audit-ready documentation and improved consistency of quality system records.
Internal Working Role Description This role is intended to provide day-to-day administrative, data, and coordination support for Quality activities tied to customer field issues, returned material, supplier failure analysis, corrective action, and quality system reporting. The position should function as the central organizer for quality case data and action tracking so Quality Engineering and management can focus on technical resolution, customer response, and systemic improvement.
Primary Internal Duties Maintain AssurX records for OBQ, FA, DOA, field RMA, CAPA, and 8D activities.Monitor open records for missing information, aging items, overdue actions, and unclear ownership.Prepare recurring Excel and Power BI trend reports for field issue activity, returned parts, supplier FA status, RMA aging, and corrective action progress.Coordinate returned part routing with ONTO Logistics and help resolve documentation or shipment-routing gaps.Prepare and distribute supplier RTV / FA instruction packages when returned material requires supplier investigation.Track engineering, factory, supplier, and field service investigation status until closure.Follow up on procedure revisions, part disposition, field service upgrade actions, stock purges, and Product Change Notice routing.Support internal ISO 9001 audit readiness by maintaining structured records, evidence files, and action tracking.

rows.title: Data Analyst, Routing and Scheduling
rows.descriptionText:
DIVISION: BPS Operations

OFFICE: Transportation Department

TEAM: Data & Strategy

ACADEMIC/NON-ACADEMIC: NON-ACADEMIC

____________________________________________________________________________________

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

rows.descriptionText:
DIVISION: BPS Operations

OFFICE: Transportation Department

TEAM: Data & Strategy

ACADEMIC/NON-ACADEMIC: NON-ACADEMIC

____________________________________________________________________________________

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

rows.title: Co-op, Data Visualization and Application Development
rows.descriptionText:
About The Role

This application is for a 6-month student role from January - June 2027. Resume review begins in October 2026.

The co-op will join the Data Visualization and Application Development (DVAD) team within Quantitative Sciences and Development Operations (QSDO). DVAD builds and supports applications, data products, and visualizations that help stakeholders consume data in an efficient way while making better informed decisions. This role is for a student who can engage with users to understand their needs, is curious about how technology can improve work, and is interested in gathering user evaluation metrics to shape a successful product.

The role will be divided across two connected areas. Some of the co-op's time will support a centralized clinical trial operations platform. The co-op will help develop an evaluation plan for gathering user feedback, support implementation of the evaluation approach, and analyze and report on responses. The goal will be to evaluate adoption, understand how the tool is being used, identify barriers or unmet needs, and recommend areas for improvement. 

The remaining time will support project management and information gathering to identify visualizations that could be useful across QSDO. This may include interviewing stakeholders, documenting business questions and user needs, organizing and synthesizing findings, tracking activities and decisions, and helping the DVAD team assess and prioritize potential visualization opportunities. 

Success will depend on curiosity, thoughtful problem solving, strong communication, attention to detail, and a user-centered perspective. Exposure to project management, survey design, analytics, research methods, or data visualization is helpful and will provide opportunities for hands-on learning with a cross-functional team. 

What You’ll Do

As a co-op you will:

Partner with the clinical operations platform team to develop an evaluation plan, including evaluation questions, target audiences, feedback methods, measures of adoption, and a practical approach for collecting and reviewing responses.  Support implementation of the evaluation plan by preparing materials, coordinating outreach, organizing responses, and maintaining clear and appropriate documentation.  Create a clear evaluation report that summarizes the approach, findings, limitations, and prioritized recommendations for future improvements. Partner with QSDO stakeholders to understand current reporting and visualization needs, existing tools, pain points, and opportunities for improvement. Plan and track small project activities, organize stakeholder input, follow up on open questions, and maintain clear documentation of decisions and next steps. Create an inventory of selected dashboards and visualizations, including their purpose, users, data sources, ownership, overlap, and gaps. 

Example Projects May Include

Clinical Operations Platform adoption and user-feedback evaluation plan. Clinical Operations Platform evaluation report with findings and prioritized improvement opportunities. QSDO visualization landscape inventory and opportunity assessment. 

Who You Are

A thoughtful and curious student who is excited by the potential of technology, applications, and data visualization to improve how people work and make decisions. Foundational understanding of research or evaluation methods, such as developing research questions, designing surveys or interview guides, collecting feedback, and recognizing bias or limitations in results. Familiarity with survey tools, spreadsheets, presentation tools, data visualization platforms, or collaboration and documentation tools is preferred. Comfortable asking questions, interviewing users, listening for underlying needs, and synthesizing information from multiple sources. Strong written and verbal communicator who can explain ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience with descriptive data analysis, and data analysis and visualization tools like R, Python, Power BI are preferred. UX Design skills are a plus. Eager to learn in a cross-functional environment and open to feedback and iteration 

To participate in the Biogen Internship or Co-op Program, students must meet the following eligibility criteria:

Legal authorization to work in the U.S. At least 18 years of age prior to the scheduled start date. Currently enrolled in an accredited community college, college, university or skills program/apprenticeship. 

Education Requirements

Currently pursuing an associate, bachelor's, or master's degree, or participating in an accredited skills program or apprenticeship. Preferred areas of study include user research, information science, public health, health informatics, social or behavioral sciences, business or data analytics, or a related interdisciplinary program.  

Job Level: Internship

Additional Information

The base compensation range for this role is: $23.00-$29.00

The actual hourly wage offered will consider the candidate’s current academic level and degree candidacy, inclusive of Associate, Bachelor’s, Master’s, JD, MD, PhD and MBA programs. It will comply with state or local minimum wage requirements specific to the job location.

In addition to compensation, Biogen offers a range of benefits designed to support our educational employees, including, but not limited to: 

Company paid holidays Commuter benefits Employee Resource Groups participation80 hours of sick time per calendar year

Why Biogen?

We are a global team with a commitment to excellence, and a pioneering spirit. As a mid-sized biotechnology company, we provide the stability and resources of a well-established business while fostering an environment where individual contributions make a significant impact. Our team encompasses some of the most talented and passionate achievers who have unparalleled opportunities for learning, growth, and expanding their skills. Department Summary:

Are you an experienced professional passionate about solving complex challenges to safeguard our nation? At MITRE, you’ll collaborate with top minds in engineering, science, and technology, leveraging cutting-edge research and experimentation to address the nation’s most pressing challenges.

DIVISION: BPS Operations

____________________________________________________________________________________

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

rows.title: Data Analyst, Routing and Scheduling
rows.descriptionText:
DIVISION: BPS Operations

OFFICE: Transportation Department

TEAM: Data & Strategy

ACADEMIC/NON-ACADEMIC: NON-ACADEMIC

____________________________________________________________________________________

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

The Boston Public Schools, in accordance with its nondiscrimination policies, does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, age, criminal record, physical or mental disability, pregnancy or pregnancy-related conditions, homelessness, sex/gender, gender identity, religion, national origin, ancestry, sexual orientation, genetics, natural or protective hairstyle, military status, immigration status, English language proficiency, or any other factor prohibited by law in its programs and activities. BPS does not tolerate any form of retaliation, or bias-based intimidation, threat or harassment that demeans individuals’ dignity or interferes with their ability to work or learn. If you require an accommodation pursuant to the ADA for the application process, please contact the Accommodations Unit at accommodations@bostonpublicschools.org.

rows.title: Biomedical Data Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
About LifeCanvas Technologies
LifeCanvas Technologies, an MIT spinoff venture, is revolutionizing the way we see and study biological systems. LifeCanvas offers cutting-edge technologies and end-to-end solutions that enable holistic molecular imaging of biological systems, accelerating breakthrough discoveries in science and the development of new therapeutic strategies. As a key partner in this global effort, our computational team works on enabling scientific innovation and directly collaborates with global researchers in bioengineering, neuroscience, and oncology.
Job SummaryWe are seeking an ambitious and motivated Biomedical Data Analyst to join our dynamic team. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience with biomedical data analysis, machine learning, or scientific computing, and a strong interest in building scalable software solutions for both research and industrial applications in a fast-paced start-up environment. In this role, you will support the analysis of large-scale 3D fluorescence microscopy datasets generated by LifeCanvas technologies. You will work closely with our tissue processing, image acquisition, and Contract Research teams to run analyses, validate outputs, troubleshoot issues, and help generate high-quality quantitative results for internal teams and external scientific partners.
Key Responsibilities:Run, validate, and troubleshoot analyses for Contract Research projects, ensuring accurate results and timely project completion.Perform quality control on analysis outputs to validate results.Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure smooth data acquisition, integration, and downstream analysis.Communicate analytical findings clearly to internal teams and external scientific partners.Assist with maintaining and improving components of LifeCanvas image-analysis pipelines for large-scale 3D fluorescence microscopy datasets.Support the development of data engineering workflows, including database management, ETL processes, and handling of large imaging datasets.
Qualifications:Bachelor’s degree in computer science, bioengineering, computational biology, electrical engineering, or a relevant field.Experience with image processing for biological and/or biomedical applicationsExperience using Python for data science, scientific computing, automation, and image analysis.Strong problem-solving skills with a self-motivated and detail-oriented mindset and the ability to work in a team environment.Adaptable and proactive in a fast-paced environment, comfortable working across multiple concurrent projects and evolving requirements.Excellent communication skills and the ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
Preferred Qualifications:Familiarity with light microscopy, neuroscience, and immunohistochemistryFamiliarity with best practices for software engineering.Exposure to machine learning or deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.Experience in working with data engineering/analysis pipelines.
Benefits:Competitive salary.Full insurance package for full-time employees.Flexible time off.401(k) benefits.

The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone.

Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and commitment to high-quality data generation.

rows.title: Secure Systems and AI Security Researcher / Engineer (Early Career)
rows.descriptionText:
The Secure Resilient Systems and Technology group advances cybersecurity research to address critical national security challenges. We develop and evaluate technologies that enable mission systems, from space and autonomous platforms to tactical communications and secure computing, to withstand cyberattack and continue the mission. Our goal is not simply to identify vulnerabilities, but to design security in from the start and provide rigorous evidence that these systems can be trusted under attack.

Our research spans secure software and embedded systems, security architecture and threat modeling, applied cryptography, formal methods, and security evaluation, as well as the intersection of AI and cybersecurity, including both AI for cybersecurity and cybersecurity for AI. We work across the R&D lifecycle, from new concepts through prototyping and transition to mission use, collaborating across Lincoln Laboratory and with government, industry, and academia.

We are a collegial and mission-driven team working on difficult problems where security, resilience, assurance, performance, and operational realities all matter. We value technical excellence, innovation, collaboration, inclusion, and individual growth. Our culture emphasizes mentoring and developing researchers into PIs and technical leaders. We strive to bring out the best in our people and our systems, so that the Laboratory and the nation can count on them when it matters most.

If you would like to pursue cutting-edge research and work on things that truly matter at a place that combines MIT's culture of academic excellence, exceptional resources, and strong work-life balance, apply here to learn more.

Job Description

As an Assistant Technical Staff member, you will:

Research, design, prototype, and evaluate new approaches to securing software, embedded, and communication systems against sophisticated cyber threats.Develop high-quality software and experimental systems using Rust, C/C++, and other languages appropriate to the research.Explore problems at the intersection of AI and cybersecurity, including applications of AI to cyber analysis and defense, as well as the security and evaluation of AI-enabled systems.Collaborate with researchers and engineers across cybersecurity, cryptography, formal methods, AI, communications, autonomy, space, and other disciplines.Present results to Laboratory and government stakeholders and contribute to reports, publications, prototypes, reusable software, and the transition of successful technologies to operational use.


Required Qualifications

To thrive in this role, you should have: 

A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Cybersecurity, Software Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.Demonstrated proficiency in at least one of the following:Software design, development, and testing in Rust (preferred), C/C++, or another systems programming language.Secure software or systems security.Systems integration, testing, and evaluation of secure systems.Embedded systems analysis, design, and implementation.Substantial hands-on technical experience beyond academic coursework, typically equivalent to at least six months of full-time technical experience, gained through internships, co-ops, research appointments, employment, or comparable experience. A significant portion must be directly relevant to cybersecurity, systems security, secure software, embedded systems, or AI security.Strong problem-solving and technical communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in teams.

Desired Experience And Expertise

We particularly value demonstrated experience in one or more of the following:

Systems engineering, security requirements analysis, and threat modeling.Security evaluation and assurance, including adversarial testing, experimental methods, security measurement, and evidence supporting security and assurance claims.Secure software development, operating system internals, embedded systems security, and network protocols.Applied cryptography and protocols, including industry and government standards.Static and dynamic software analysis and applied formal methods.AI and cybersecurity, including AI-enabled software analysis, vulnerability discovery, security testing, threat analysis, and cyber defense; and security of AI-enabled systems, including adversarial threats and evaluation of security, robustness, and resilience.Technical communication, including documenting designs, writing reports and research papers, and presenting technical results.


We do not expect candidates to have expertise in all of these areas and welcome candidates interested in developing deeper expertise through hands-on research.

Recent Graduate Hiring Range: $100,200 - $120,000

Experienced Hiring Range: $100,200 - $150,000

 Disclaimer: MIT Lincoln Laboratory provides a typical hiring range as a good faith estimate of what we reasonably expect to offer for this position at the time of posting. The final salary offered to a selected candidate will depend on various factors, including—but not limited to—the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate’s experience, skills and education/training, internal equity considerations and applicable legal requirements. This range reflects base salary only and does not include additional forms of compensation or benefits.

At MIT Lincoln Laboratory, our exceptional career opportunities include many outstanding benefits to help you stay healthy, feel supported, and enjoy a fulfilling work-life balance. Benefits offered to employees include:

Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plansMIT-funded pensionMatching 401KPaid leave (including vacation, sick, parental, military, etc.)Tuition reimbursement and continuing education programsMentorship programsA range of work-life balance options... and much more! 


Please visit our Benefits page for more information. As an employee of MIT, you can also take advantage of other voluntary benefits, discounts and perks .

Selected candidate will be subject to a pre-employment background investigation and must be able to obtain and maintain a Secret level DoD security clearance.

Job Title

Usability Designer

Job Description

As a Usability Designer within Philips' Ambulatory Monitoring & Diagnostics (AM&D) business, you will play a critical role in shaping products that improve patient outcomes and clinician experiences around the world. You'll champion user-centered design, ensuring our solutions are safe, effective, and intuitive while advocating for the needs of patients, caregivers, and healthcare professionals across a global portfolio of innovative products and services.

Your Role

You're The Right Fit If

We are a health technology company. We built our entire company around the belief that every human matters, and we won't stop until everybody everywhere has access to the quality healthcare that we all deserve. Do the work of your life to help improve the lives of others.

Learn more about our business.Discover our rich and exciting history.Learn more about our purpose.Learn more about our culture.

REPORTS TO: Assistant Director of Data Management

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Boston Public Schools Office of Transportation is one of the largest departments in the district overseeing a nearly $200M annual budget (~12% of total spending). The Transportation office provides over 600 buses that transport nearly 20,000 students across the district as well as local parochial, private and charter schools. This is one of the largest and most complex school bus transportation systems in the country. The Data Analyst for Routing and Scheduling works within the BPSDOT Data Team providing technology system management, fleet schedule assembly and management, and reporting and data analysis to support overall effective and efficient routing and fleet scheduling.

Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Manage data in all software systems related to routing and ensure data is properly synced with external data sources. Implement data auditing strategies and processes to ensure data integrity

Fleet schedule assembly and management

Create and maintain fleet schedule that balances performance and efficiencyAssist with optimization and troubleshooting of routes

Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service. They must also continuously seek input from a diverse set of perspectives and think critically about the impact of their work. Communication – This is one of the most important skills to have when working in a team environment. Being able to clearly convey your thoughts/ideas to any audience is vital to the success of this position. We need someone who can explain highly technical things to anyone. 

Terms: Managerial, C53. City of Boston Residency is Required.

BPS does not tolerate any form of retaliation, or bias-based intimidation, threat or harassment that demeans individuals’ dignity or interferes with their ability to work or learn. If you require an accommodation pursuant to the ADA for the application process, please contact the Accommodations Unit at accommodations@bostonpublicschools.org.

rows.title: Intermediate Modeling and Simulation / Operations Research Analyst
rows.descriptionText:
At MITRE, your passion fuels work that impacts our nation and improves lives. This is where your skills strengthen national security, cybersecurity, health, transportation, and citizen services. We’re a nonprofit engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization working in the public interest. With objectivity and integrity at our core, we lead federally funded research and development centers for U.S. government agencies – collaborating with industry and academia to deliver integrated, high-impact solutions that advance our nation’s health, security, and prosperity. Our people tackle the toughest technical challenges, supported by competitive benefits, meaningful career development, and a culture of innovation, collaboration, and technical excellence. Choose MITRE for a career with purpose — and help shape the future.

Department Summary:

Shape the Future of National Security—Join MITRE and Tackle the Toughest Challenges with Innovation and Impact!

Are you an experienced professional passionate about solving complex challenges to safeguard our nation? At MITRE, you’ll collaborate with top minds in engineering, science, and technology, leveraging cutting-edge research and experimentation to address the nation’s most pressing challenges.

MITRE is a nonprofit systems engineering, applied research, and advanced technology organization that operates federally funded R&D centers to deliver deep technical and systems integration, rapid prototype development, and mission-driven innovation in the public interest. Headquarters are in McLean, Virginia and Bedford, Massachusetts are supported by over 60 sites across the U.S. and globe to bring solutions to the field.

MITRE Technology and Engineering Modeling and Analysis (M&A) Division brings together researchers, autonomy engineers, mission specialists, and systems experts to translate advanced research into operationally relevant solutions. M&A is seeking modeling and simulation engineers and operations research analysts to support the operations analysis and complex systems modeling work across MITRE’s national security and public sector missions.

Roles & Responsibilities:

We are seeking an experienced, highly motivated Modeling & Simulation / Operations Research Analyst to support critical national security missions. In this role, you will partner with operational stakeholders to develop and apply advanced modeling, simulation, and analytical tools—integrating mathematics, physics, engineering, and programming—to generate actionable insights for mission and sponsor needs.

You will tackle complex, real-world problems at the intersection of technology and national security while expanding your skills through hands-on work. We value curiosity, innovation, and a passion for learning, and we’re looking for candidates who thrive in collaborative, diverse teams and are committed to delivering solutions that make a real impact.

Responsibilities include:

Contribute to the development and application of modeling and simulation tools by providing technical expertise and support.Collaborate with multidisciplinary teams to refine methodologies and address technical challenges.Shape project strategies by identifying and recommending innovative techniques and tools to improve modeling, simulation, and analysis capabilities.Communicate findings and recommendations to stakeholders to ensure alignment with mission goals.Support collaboration across teams to enhance the effectiveness and scalability of modeling, simulation, and analysis initiatives.

Basic Qualifications:

Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 2 years of related experience; or an advanced degree with relevant experience who can immediately contribute at this job step; or equivalent combination of related education and work experience.Experience with operational analysis tools (e.g., AFSIM, STK, NGTS, STORM)Experience with developing and debugging physics-based modeling and simulation tools to address research questions.Experience in conducting quantitative analysis of simulation results to identify key focus areas and extract critical lessons learned.Experienced in presenting analysis to non-technical audiences and senior leaders, and bridging operational teams with technical experts to create mission-focused solutions.Demonstrated proficiency in programming languages and applications such as C/C++, Java, Julia, Python, MATLAB, or MathematicaActive Secret Clearance (Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance)Must have an active Secret U.S Government issued Security Clearance and must be eligible to obtain and maintain a Top Secret/SCI U.S Government issued Security Clearance. Per the U.S. Government’s eligibility requirements, you must be a U.S Citizen to be considered for a security clearance.The position requires a minimum of 4 days on site

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience in mission engineering, including interpreting and analyzing mission threadsExperience with data analysis and data visualization tools or environmentsSkilled in presenting technical material through reports and presentations, with strong problem-solving and communication abilities, and a passion for collaborating with experts across various disciplines.Desire to learn new techniques and approaches on-the-job by leveraging structured educational content, as well as expertise from team members.Hands-on experience in adapting research done in academia and industry to "real-world" challenging data sources and problems setsActive DoD Top Secret clearance with access to Secure Compartmented Information (TS/SCI).

This requisition requires the candidate to have a minimum of the following clearance(s):

Secret

This requisition requires the hired candidate to have or obtain, within one year from the date of hire, the following clearance(s):

Top Secret/SCI

$98,800 - $123,500 - $148,200 Annual

Onsite

Moderna is seeking a Research Associate for a position based at the Norwood, MA site. This individual will contribute to the development, refinement, and implementation of cell-based bioassays supporting release and stability testing for mRNA therapeutics and vaccines. Site: The General Hospital Corporation

Mass General Brigham relies on a wide range of professionals, including doctors, nurses, business people, tech experts, researchers, and systems analysts to advance our mission. As a not-for-profit, we support patient care, research, teaching, and community service, striving to provide exceptional care. Job Summary

Overview Position

We are seeking a scientifically motivated individual for a pre-Ph.D./M.S. research opportunity within the MGH Hepatology research environment. This is a one-year appointment with the possibility of a one-to-two-year extension, emphasizing training and the acquisition of advanced biological and computational skills. The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative team, work under the direct mentorship of Principal Investigator Prof. Nadia Alatrakchi and learn essential skills for a future career in science.

Our laboratory studies immune cell populations in the setting of human disease, with a particular focus on innate immunity. The Channing/Harvard Cohorts Biorepository (CHCB) manages sample collection, storage, and distribution for some of the world’s largest and most intensively studied longitudinal cohorts, including the Nurses’ Health Studies, Health Professionals Follow-up Study, Growing Up Today Study, and Physicians’ Health Study I. Responsibilities:

Technology System Management:

Maintain technology systems related to routing (e.g., Zum, Geotab) and adapt these systems to shifting business needsServe as primary liaison with vendors to ensure BPS DOT is:Using the most appropriate version of softwareUtilizing the software to its fullest potentialUp to date on training all necessary staffServe as liaison between the BPS routing team, BPS Technology and transportation contractorsDevelop and run queries to perform data extractions needed by teams in the department from various data sources including the routing system as well as the district's student information system. Reporting and data analysis 

Gather and translate user requirements into technical specificationsDevelop and generate reports and dashboards for various stakeholders such as BPSDOT staff, the Executive Director of Transportation, COO, Superintendent and Mayors OfficePerform complex analyses on routing data to improve efficiency and bus performanceCollaboration with operational department managers (e.g. Operations, Customer Service, Monitors Unit)Understand operational complexities as they relate to routing and incorporate into data flows and checksSupport training of other departmental staff on how to use routing and fleet data and technology to improve operational proceduresParticipate in strategy setting and development for the Transportation Department

Qualifications - Required:

A Bachelor's Degree or higher in a quantitative field such as Mathematics, Engineering, Actuarial, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or similar field1+ years working in a data management/ technological systems maintenance capacityExpert analytical skills, demonstrating a mastery of Python or R, SQL, and either Microsoft Excel or Google SheetsStrong understanding of data warehousing principles and methodologiesAbility to create project plans / timelines, collecting input from stakeholders and sharing back outputsStrong written and oral communication skills, in particular the ability to explain data systems and analyses to non-technical audienceHighly organized and detail oriented

Qualifications - Preferred:

Candidates should have a demonstrated history of infusing the following traits into their work:

Curiosity - We need people to help our organization drive improvement. We feel that this requires a healthy desire to discover how and why things work the way they do. We also want candidates to be able to look for those explanations in data. Quantitative Orientation – Some people think that everything is measurable, that all information can have a more precise and reliable measurement. This is who we want on our team; someone whose approach to everything is rigorous, inquisitive, and analytical. Persistence – You will have to deal with messy datasets and new and evolving problems in an operation that is learning how to use data effectively. We need you to be able to work through a problem until it is solved, not until you reach a road block. Vision – This role is about more than just using quantitative skills to answer other people’s questions. We need someone who can help identify problems and opportunities, and who knows how to ask the right questions to address them. Technical Skills – If quantitative orientation is about a candidate’s will to use data, this trait is about the skill. We need someone who is trained in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and/or economics. But we also want someone who is constantly acquiring technical skills and understands the value of a multidisciplinary approach to problem solving. Teamwork – We believe that excellent teams, composed of high-performing team members, can have an enormous impact. New team members are valued for their diverse experiences and commitment to service.
